first_impression: This looks lovely. The low-poly highland valley at golden hour, the felt-and-serif UI and the border collie with a dashed herding ring all say cosy and confident, and the season map with ten named evenings tells me straight away that there is somewhere to go. My worry is that from the top-down play camera a lot of the evenings turn into the same mustard lawn with tiny white blobs on it, and the wolf moments get buried under foreground pines.
best_things: The title screen and the low view (e1-low-view.jpg), with the river, the bridge, the faceted rock and Pip mid-gallop, are screenshots that would make me click on an itch page.

The season map (season-map.jpg, season-map-after-1.jpg), with ten named evenings from midsummer to first snow plus charms, ribbons, Wolf Moon stars and a daily 'Saturday's Evening', is real progression and a reason to come back tomorrow.

Each evening adds one clear new idea: lambs that follow their mothers, a ram you have to stare down, a judged trial with gates in order, mist where you go by bleats. Old Angus with his name tag and orange horns (evening-4-angus.jpg) reads instantly.

worst_problems.problem: In the wolf moment the bottom third of the screen is a dark wall of foreground pines, and the wolf, the thing I most need to see, is a small purple shape inside that canopy, half under the controls bar. The banner says 'A wolf is stalking your flock!' but my eyes go to the empty meadow.
worst_problems.suggestion: Frame the camera so the wolf sits in open ground, or fade out the trees between me and the wolf. Never let the threat sit under the HUD bar.

worst_problems.problem: From the play camera most places look like the same ochre-mustard field with scattered purple heather dots. The trial is a flat striped lawn with five sheep and two gate posts and almost nothing else in view, and the corrie's heather is spread evenly like wallpaper.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give each place a different ground colour and some landmarks in the playfield. Put the trial crowd, judges' tent and bunting where I can see them while I play, and clump the heather into patches instead of sprinkling it.

worst_problems.problem: The small animals are hard to tell apart. Old Fly is a grey smudge glued to Pip's side. The lambs are barely smaller than the ewes. In the mist the flock are faceless white lumps that I first took for boulders.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give Fly a distinct coat colour and a small name tag, make the lambs clearly tiny and bouncy, and keep the sheep's dark faces visible even in fog.

worst_problems.problem: The evening cards are walls of text. A story paragraph, a 'new tonight' box, a 'new wolves' box, star thresholds, a ribbon, a best score and a six-charm grid all come before Begin. I would skim it and then not know how the ram or the old grey wolf works.
worst_problems.suggestion: Cut each mechanic to one line with a little icon, and teach the rest in the level with a short prompt the first time it happens.

worst_problems.problem: The star goals in the first evening are '7 home, 8, all 8', so two stars and three stars are the same goal. On the season map after evening 1, a Wolf Moon badge is drawn over the 'MIDSUMMER' label on the first card.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make every star a different goal (for example a time or a no-losses condition for the third), and move the badge so it doesn't sit on top of the text.

boredom_points: The Glenbrae Trial looks like five sheep on an empty mown field with a timer. Without a crowd or anything else going on, it would feel like a driving test.
Every evening ends with pushing a clump into the same rectangular stone fold. If the fold and the approach look the same each time, the last minute of every level will blur together.
With the camera this high, Pip and the sheep are small, so long stretches of walking behind the flock across a big field could get monotonous.
confusions: In e1-herding.jpg the counter says '4 home, need 7' and 'hurry: 3 more to go before dark'. That works out, but the dots row with a separate dot after the bar was not obvious until I counted.
In e1-low-view.jpg there is a dashed white line on the ground running towards the sheep. Is it a path, a route hint, or something a wolf is doing?
In evening-3-lambing.jpg the house and wolf edge markers sit on top of the bottom controls bar, so it is hard to tell which direction they point.
In evening-3-lambing.jpg there is a yellow glowing smudge on the grass on the left with nothing on it. I could not tell what it was.
On the cards for evenings 3, 4, 5 and 7 it says 'Your best: 2 stars' even though the season map shows those evenings as locked, so I was not sure what had been played.
wish_list: A free-play or sandbox field where I can just practise herding with no timer.
A replay or photo mode for that gorgeous low camera at sunset.
More life in the trial: a crowd, a commentator line, a score breakdown per gate.
Pip cosmetics I can actually see from the top-down camera (collars, coat colours).
A leaderboard or shared seed for the daily evening so I can compare with friends.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, gentle sheepdog game with a real season to work through, let down by a camera that sometimes hides the wolves in the trees and evenings that start to look like the same mustard field.
